theoryOfChange: The Family & Youth Institute (thefyi.org) explicitly mentions 'the fyi's theory of change' on their Research page. They describe their approach as a community-based participatory research model that ensures projects are grounded in community spirit and collaboration. This involves partnering with communities to identify priorities and needs, engaging and integrating community voices throughout the research process, incorporating community perspectives on data, identifying practical solutions, and sharing the benefits. This outlines how their activities lead to impact.

rich_narrative.summary: The Family and Youth Institute (The FYI) is a research-focused organization dedicated to strengthening the Muslim community through mental health education and youth development. founded in 2006, the organization addresses critical community needs by translating complex research into practical resources for families and leaders. In <cite id="2">FY2023, the organization reported total revenue of $850,837</cite>, though it experienced a significant <cite id="2">revenue decline to $497,120 in FY2024</cite>. Despite this contraction, the charity maintains a <cite id="1">90/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>, reflecting a high standard of accountability. The FYI operates primarily as a capacity-building entity, providing <cite id="5">research studies on resiliency and prevention</cite> to empower local communities. Its work is characterized by a <cite id="5">strong theory of change</cite> that bridges the gap between academic research and community-based practice. While the organization is lean, it demonstrates <cite id="1">efficient fundraising operations</cite>, spending only <cite id="1">$0.08 to raise every $1</cite>. This efficiency ensures that a significant portion of donor contributions supports its <cite id="5">core programs in marriage support, parenting, and youth development</cite>. As a <cite id="6">zakat-eligible organization</cite>, it provides a specialized avenue for Muslim donors to support mental health advocacy and community wellness.
